You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.

AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

slug: aflfast
title: "AFLFast: Power Schedules via Markov Chain Model"
description: |
  Implement AFLFast's power schedules based on modeling fuzzing as a Markov chain.
  Each unique execution path is a state; mutations cause transitions between states.
  The key insight is that AFL's constant energy wastes effort on high-frequency paths.
  AFLFast assigns energy inversely proportional to path frequency f(i) and exponentially
  in selection count s(i). Includes: EXPLOIT schedule (p(i)=alpha, same as AFL),
  EXPLORE schedule (p(i)=alpha/beta, normalized), COE schedule (cut-off exponential:
  skip seeds with f(i)>mu, otherwise min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i), M)), FAST schedule
  (recommended: min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i) / f(i), M)), LINEAR schedule (min(alpha/beta *
  s(i)/f(i), M)), QUAD schedule (min(alpha/beta * s(i)^2/f(i), M)). Also implements
  PathFrequencyTracker (Markov state identification, transition counting, rare path
  detection), seed prioritization strategies (prioritize_small_s for FAST/COE,
  prioritize_small_f for explore/linear/quad), EnergyComputer with Gini coefficient
  analysis, and schedule comparison utilities.
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/aflfast_schedules.py
  - fuzzsim/aflfast_search.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflfast_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - Markov chain path model
  - path frequency tracking (f(i) = inputs exercising path i)
  - selection count tracking (s(i) = times seed i was chosen)
  - power schedule variants (FAST, COE, explore, exploit, linear, quad)
  - energy assignment formulas (exponential, linear, quadratic)
  - cut-off mechanism (skip over-fuzzed seeds)
  - upper bound M on energy (prevent explosion)
  - seed prioritization by s(i) and f(i)
  - Markov state transitions and probability estimation
  - rare path identification and bonus
  - energy distribution analysis (Gini coefficient)
expected_outputs:
  AFLFAST_PATHS_FAST: 10
  AFLFAST_PATHS_COE: 10
  AFLFAST_SPEEDUP: 1.00
  AFLFAST_MEAN_ENERGY: 198.5
slug: aflgo
title: "AFLGo: Directed Greybox Fuzzing"
description: |
  Implement AFLGo's directed greybox fuzzing with distance-based seed prioritization
  and simulated annealing for exploration-to-exploitation transition. Two-level distance
  computation: (1) Function-level via BFS on reverse call graph from target functions,
  (2) Basic-block level combining CFG shortest paths with function distances via harmonic
  mean. CallGraph class with function/edge management. CFGDistance class with BFS-based
  shortest path computation. Distance normalization to [0,1] range. Seed distance via
  minimum block distance among covered edges. Simulated annealing with exponential cooling
  schedule T(t)=T0*alpha^(t/t_x*K), plus alternative cooling schedules (linear: T0*(1-t/t_x),
  logarithmic: T0/(1+log(1+t/t_x*K)), adaptive: adjusts alpha based on progress). Energy
  assignment formula: p(s,T)=base*((1-d(s))*(1-T)+0.5*T) transitioning from uniform (T=1)
  to distance-proportional (T=0). Seed skipping during exploitation phase (T<0.3, d>0.9).
  DistanceComputer class orchestrating the full pipeline. Phase detection (exploration/
  transition/exploitation).
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/aflgo_distance.py
  - fuzzsim/aflgo_annealing.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflgo_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - directed greybox fuzzing
  - call graph construction and BFS traversal
  - CFG shortest path computation
  - function-level distance via reverse BFS
  - basic-block level distance via harmonic mean
  - distance normalization to [0,1]
  - seed distance aggregation (minimum, harmonic mean)
  - simulated annealing (exponential cooling)
  - alternative cooling schedules (linear, logarithmic, adaptive)
  - exploration vs exploitation phases
  - temperature-based energy assignment
  - seed skipping during exploitation
  - time-to-exposure (TTE) metric
expected_outputs:
  AFLGO_DISTANCE_ACCURACY: 100.0
  AFLGO_DIRECTED_TTE: 939
  AFLGO_UNDIRECTED_TTE: 1103
  AFLGO_SPEEDUP: 1.17

slug: aflpp
title: "AFL++: Modular Fuzzing Framework"
description: |
  Implement AFL++'s modular framework with full custom mutator API and MOpt PSO-based
  mutation scheduling. Custom Mutator API matching AFL++ afl-fuzz-mutator.c: init(),
  fuzz(buf, add_buf), fuzz_count(buf), havoc_mutation(buf, max_size),
  havoc_mutation_probability(), post_process(buf), trim(buf), describe(),
  queue_new_entry(buf, coverage). MutatorRegistry: register/unregister mutators,
  weighted random selection, dynamic weight adjustment (1.1x on success, 0.99x on
  failure, min 0.1). Built-in mutators: GrammarMutator (token templates, structured
  input generation, grammar-aware trimming), CmpLogMutator (RedQueen comparison
  operand recording and substitution for bypassing magic bytes). MOpt PSO scheduler:
  pilot phase (independent operator testing, L iterations each), core phase (PSO
  velocity update: v=w*v+c1*r1*(pbest-x)+c2*r2*(gbest-x), position update: x=x+v,
  velocity clamping [-0.3, 0.3], probability bounds [0.02, 0.50], normalization to
  valid distribution). Operator set: bit_flip, byte_flip, arith_add, arith_sub,
  interesting, random_byte, havoc_1, havoc_2. Personal/global best tracking, fitness
  history, convergence monitoring. PowerScheduleEnsemble: rotate through FAST/COE/
  EXPLORE/QUAD/LIN schedules per queue cycle.
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/aflpp_custom_mutator.py
  - fuzzsim/aflpp_mopt.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflpp_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - custom mutator API (init, fuzz, describe, trim, havoc_mutation, post_process, queue_new_entry)
  - mutator registry with dynamic weighted selection
  - grammar-based mutation (token templates)
  - CmpLog/RedQueen (comparison operand replacement)
  - Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for operator selection
  - PSO velocity/position update equations
  - pilot phase (independent operator testing)
  - core phase (continuous PSO optimization)
  - inertia weight, cognitive/social components
  - velocity clamping and probability bounds
  - personal best and global best tracking
  - operator success rate monitoring
  - dynamic probability adjustment
  - PowerScheduleEnsemble (schedule rotation)
expected_outputs:
  AFLPP_CUSTOM_MUTATOR_PATHS: 10
  AFLPP_MOPT_PATHS: 10
  AFLPP_MOPT_IMPROVEMENT: 0.0
  AFLPP_TOTAL_COVERAGE: 86.7
slug: fairfuzz
title: "FairFuzz: Targeted Mutation for Rare Branches"
description: |
  Implement FairFuzz's approach to improving coverage of rare branches by identifying
  under-covered edges, detecting input-to-branch influence via differential mutation,
  and applying targeted mutations that preserve rare branch hits. Rare branch
  identification: count seeds per edge, edges with count <= threshold are "rare".
  Both fixed threshold (absolute cutoff) and dynamic threshold (percentile of hit count
  distribution) supported. RareBranchTracker with incremental updates and statistics.
  Influence detection (mutation masking): for each byte position, probe with random
  replacements and measure whether target branch coverage is destroyed. If >60% of
  probes destroy coverage, the byte is "influential" and must be preserved. Fast
  variant with early termination. InfluenceDetector class with caching (hash-based
  cache key: data_hash + target_branch). Masked mutation: apply havoc-like operations
  only to safe (non-influential) positions while preserving critical bytes. Branch
  selection strategy: prefer rare branches already hit by the seed (preservation is
  meaningful), among candidates pick the rarest. Rarity scores normalized to [0,1]
  for weighted targeting.
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/fairfuzz_rare.py
  - fuzzsim/fairfuzz_mask.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/fairfuzz_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - rare branch identification (edges hit by few seeds)
  - edge frequency tracking per corpus
  - fixed vs dynamic rarity threshold (percentile-based)
  - RareBranchTracker with incremental updates
  - probe-based influence detection (differential mutation)
  - statistical threshold for influence (>60% probes destroy coverage)
  - mutation masking (preserving critical byte positions)
  - InfluenceDetector with hash-based caching
  - targeted havoc with position constraints
  - branch selection strategy (prefer seed's own rare branches)
  - rarity score normalization
expected_outputs:

  FAIRFUZZ_RARE_COVERAGE: 50.0
  FAIRFUZZ_TOTAL_COVERAGE: 86.7
  FAIRFUZZ_IMPROVEMENT: 0.0

1	"""AFL (American Fuzzy Lop) core fuzzer simulation.
2	
3	A faithful reimplementation of AFL's core mechanisms on top of the fuzzsim
4	target model:
5	
6	- 64KB shared-memory bitmap with hit-count bucketing (``classify_counts``)
7	- edge coverage hashing via ``(prev_block XOR cur_block) >> 1``
8	- fork server simulation (``ForkServer``) with an execution counter
9	- test case calibration (multi-run stability detection, average exec time)
10	- input trimming (powers-of-two block removal preserving coverage)
11	- corpus culling via greedy set cover (smallest+fastest seed per edge)
12	- full deterministic stages in AFL order: walking bitflip 1/2/4 bits,
13	  byte flip 8/16/32 bits, arithmetic add/sub 1..35 for 8/16/32-bit widths
14	  (both endianness), interesting values 8/16/32 (both endianness),
15	  dictionary insertion (user tokens + auto-dictionary extracted during the
16	  bitflip stage when a byte value change produced new coverage)
17	- havoc stage with 2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations per iteration
18	- splice stage (midpoint combination of two queue entries, then havoc)
19	- performance scoring (``calculate_score``) from exec speed, coverage size,
20	  depth and stability
21	- constant power schedule (fixed energy per seed, AFL-style)
22	- crash deduplication via coverage hash (hash of the crashing edge set)
23	- queue scheduling with favored-seed priority (75% skip of non-favored
24	  seeds, 25% fuzz them anyway)
25	
26	All randomness flows through a single ``np.random.RandomState`` instance so
27	runs are fully deterministic given the seed.
28	"""
29	
30	import hashlib
31	from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
32	
33	import numpy as np
34	
35	from fuzzsim.bitmap import CoverageBitmap, MAP_SIZE
36	from fuzzsim.mutation import (
37	    INTERESTING_8,
38	    INTERESTING_16,
39	    INTERESTING_32,
40	    bit_flip,
41	    byte_flip,
42	    splice,
43	)
44	from fuzzsim.seed import TestCase
45	
46	ARITH_MAX = 35  # AFL arithmetic stage uses values 1..35
47	SKIP_NONFAVORED_PROB = 0.75  # 75% chance to skip a non-favored seed
48	CALIBRATION_RUNS = 3  # calibration executions per new test case
49	MAX_AUTO_DICT_TOKENS = 128  # cap on auto-extracted dictionary tokens
50	
51	# Interesting value tables per operand width (in bytes), as in AFL.
52	INTERESTING_BY_WIDTH = {
53	    1: INTERESTING_8,
54	    2: INTERESTING_16,
55	    4: INTERESTING_32,
56	}

58	
59	def classify_counts(counts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
60	    """Bucket raw hit counts the way AFL's ``classify_counts`` does.
61	
62	    Buckets: 1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+. Zero stays zero.
63	    The bucket id reported for a range is the range's lower bound encoded
64	    as in AFL's bucket shift table (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 respectively).
65	    """
66	    counts = np.asarray(counts)
67	    out = np.zeros(counts.shape, dtype=np.uint8)
68	    out[counts == 1] = 1
69	    out[counts == 2] = 2
70	    out[counts == 3] = 3
71	    out[(counts >= 4) & (counts <= 7)] = 4
72	    out[(counts >= 8) & (counts <= 15)] = 5
73	    out[(counts >= 16) & (counts <= 31)] = 6
74	    out[(counts >= 32) & (counts <= 127)] = 7
75	    out[counts >= 128] = 8
76	    return out

79	def edge_hash(prev_block: int, cur_block: int) -> int:
80	    """Hash a CFG edge into the 64KB bitmap: (prev XOR cur) >> 1."""
81	    return ((prev_block ^ cur_block) >> 1) % MAP_SIZE

84	class ForkServerResult:
85	    """Result of a single fork-server execution."""
86	
87	    __slots__ = ("edges", "classified", "is_crash", "exec_time")
88	
89	    def __init__(self, edges: Set[int], classified: np.ndarray,
90	                 is_crash: bool, exec_time: float):
91	        self.edges = edges
92	        self.classified = classified  # bucketed 64KB bitmap (np.uint8 array)
93	        self.is_crash = is_crash
94	        self.exec_time = exec_time

97	class ForkServer:
98	    """Simulates AFL's fork server.
99	
100	    Executes the target on demand, keeps an execution counter, and reports
101	    coverage both as an exact edge set and as a classified 64KB bitmap
102	    (edge ids are mapped into the bitmap via ``edge_hash`` when the target
103	    exposes CFG block information, otherwise by edge id).
104	    """
105	
106	    def __init__(self, target):
107	        self.target = target
108	        self.exec_count = 0
109	        self._edge_index: Dict[int, int] = {}
110	        program = getattr(target, "program", None)
111	        if program is not None:
112	            for edge in program.edges:
113	                self._edge_index[edge.edge_id] = edge_hash(edge.src, edge.dst)
114	
115	    def bitmap_index(self, edge_id: int) -> int:
116	        """Return the bitmap index for an edge id."""
117	        return self._edge_index.get(edge_id, edge_id % MAP_SIZE)
118	
119	    def run(self, data: bytes) -> ForkServerResult:
120	        """Execute the target once and classify the hit counts."""
121	        self.exec_count += 1
122	        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.target.execute(data)
123	        counts = np.zeros(MAP_SIZE, dtype=np.uint8)
124	        for edge_id in edges:
125	            idx = self.bitmap_index(edge_id)
126	            counts[idx] = min(255, counts[idx] + 1)
127	        return ForkServerResult(edges, classify_counts(counts),
128	                                is_crash, exec_time)

131	class AFLFuzzer:
132	    """Core AFL fuzzer driving a simulated target.
133	
134	    Parameters:
135	        target: program under test (must provide ``execute(bytes)``).
136	        seeds: initial corpus inputs.
137	        rng: ``np.random.RandomState`` used for ALL randomness.
138	        havoc_energy: fixed energy (havoc iterations) per scheduled seed;
139	            this is the constant power schedule.
140	        splice_energy: splice iterations per scheduled seed (from cycle 1).
141	        max_input_len: cap on mutated input length.
142	        enable_trimming: run powers-of-two trimming before deterministic
143	            stages (AFL default behavior; can be disabled per experiment).
144	        calibration_runs: executions per calibration.
145	        skip_nonfavored_prob: probability of skipping a non-favored seed.
146	    """
147	
148	    def __init__(self, target, seeds: List[bytes],
149	                 rng: Optional[np.random.RandomState] = None,
150	                 havoc_energy: int = 16, splice_energy: int = 4,
151	                 max_input_len: int = 1024, enable_trimming: bool = True,
152	                 calibration_runs: int = CALIBRATION_RUNS,
153	                 skip_nonfavored_prob: float = SKIP_NONFAVORED_PROB):
154	        self.target = target
155	        self.rng = rng if rng is not None else np.random.RandomState(0)
156	        self.havoc_energy = havoc_energy
157	        self.splice_energy = splice_energy
158	        self.max_input_len = max_input_len
159	        self.enable_trimming = enable_trimming
160	        self.calibration_runs = calibration_runs
161	        self.skip_nonfavored_prob = skip_nonfavored_prob
162	
163	        self.fork_server = ForkServer(target)
164	        self.bitmap = CoverageBitmap()
165	        # OR of all admitted classified bitmaps: a bucket pattern counts as
166	        # "new coverage" if it sets a byte never seen before.
167	        self._seen_classified = np.zeros(MAP_SIZE, dtype=np.uint8)
168	
169	        self.queue: List[TestCase] = []
170	        self.crashes: Dict[str, TestCase] = {}  # coverage hash -> crash TC
171	        self.user_dict: List[bytes] = []
172	        self.auto_dict: List[bytes] = []
173	        self.current_cycle = 0
174	        self.scores: Dict[int, float] = {}  # id(tc) -> calculate_score value
175	
176	        for seed in seeds:
177	            self._load_initial_seed(seed)
178	        self.cull_queue()
179	
180	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
181	    # Corpus / reporting properties
182	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
183	
184	    @property
185	    def paths_discovered(self) -> int:
186	        """Total number of queue entries (paths) discovered."""
187	        return len(self.queue)
188	
189	    @property
190	    def corpus_size(self) -> int:
191	        """Corpus size after culling bookkeeping (culling marks favored
192	        seeds but never removes entries, so this equals paths)."""
193	        return len(self.queue)
194	
195	    @property
196	    def unique_crashes(self) -> int:
197	        """Number of deduplicated crashes."""
198	        return len(self.crashes)
199	
200	    @property
201	    def exec_count(self) -> int:
202	        return self.fork_server.exec_count
203	
204	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
205	    # Calibration, trimming, culling
206	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
207	
208	    def calibrate_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
209	        """Run a test case multiple times to measure stability.
210	
211	        Stores the average execution time and flags the case as variable
212	        if the classified coverage differs between runs.
213	        """
214	        signatures = []
215	        times = []
216	        for _ in range(self.calibration_runs):
217	            res = self.fork_server.run(tc.data)
218	            signatures.append(res.classified.tobytes())
219	            times.append(res.exec_time)
220	        tc.exec_time = sum(times) / len(times) if times else 0.0
221	        # Dynamic attribute: TestCase has no stability field of its own.
222	        tc.is_variable = len(set(signatures)) > 1  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
223	
224	    def trim_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
225	        """Powers-of-two block removal trimming.
226	
227	        Try removing blocks of size len/2, len/4, ... down to 1 byte. A
228	        removal is kept only if the classified coverage is preserved.
229	        """
230	        data = tc.data
231	        if len(data) < 5:
232	            return
233	        reference = self.fork_server.run(data)
234	        if reference.is_crash:
235	            return
236	        ref_sig = reference.classified.tobytes()
237	
238	        shift = 1
239	        while (len(data) >> shift) >= 1:
240	            block = len(data) >> shift
241	            pos = 0
242	            while pos < len(data):
243	                end = min(pos + block, len(data))
244	                candidate = data[:pos] + data[end:]
245	                if candidate:
246	                    res = self.fork_server.run(candidate)
247	                    if (not res.is_crash
248	                            and res.classified.tobytes() == ref_sig):
249	                        data = candidate
250	                        continue  # retry at same position with shifted data
251	                pos += block
252	            shift += 1
253	        if data != tc.data:
254	            tc.data = data
255	
256	    def cull_queue(self) -> None:
257	        """Greedy set cover: for each covered edge pick the smallest and
258	        fastest queue entry covering it. Those entries are marked favored
259	        and their ``unique_edges`` set is updated."""
260	        best_for_edge: Dict[int, TestCase] = {}
261	        for edge_id in sorted(self.bitmap.global_coverage):
262	            best: Optional[TestCase] = None
263	            for tc in self.queue:
264	                if edge_id in tc.coverage:
265	                    if (best is None
266	                            or (tc.size, tc.exec_time) < (best.size,
267	                                                          best.exec_time)):
268	                        best = tc
269	            if best is not None:
270	                best_for_edge[edge_id] = best
271	
272	        favored = set(best_for_edge.values())
273	        for tc in self.queue:
274	            tc.is_favored = tc in favored
275	            tc.unique_edges = {e for e, b in best_for_edge.items() if b is tc}
276	
277	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
278	    # Scoring and power schedule
279	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
280	
281	    def calculate_score(self, tc: TestCase) -> float:
282	        """AFL-style performance score based on exec speed, coverage size,
283	        depth and stability. Higher is better."""
284	        if not self.queue:
285	            return 100.0
286	        avg_exec = sum(t.exec_time for t in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
287	        avg_cov = sum(len(t.coverage) for t in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
288	
289	        score = 100.0
290	        # Execution speed relative to the corpus average.
291	        if avg_exec > 0:
292	            ratio = tc.exec_time / avg_exec
293	            if ratio > 10:
294	                score *= 0.25
295	            elif ratio > 4:
296	                score *= 0.5
297	            elif ratio > 2:
298	                score *= 0.75
299	            elif ratio < 0.25:
300	                score *= 3.0
301	            elif ratio < 0.5:
302	                score *= 2.0
303	            elif ratio < 0.75:
304	                score *= 1.5
305	        # Coverage size relative to the corpus average.
306	        if avg_cov > 0:
307	            cratio = len(tc.coverage) / avg_cov
308	            if cratio > 3:
309	                score *= 4.0
310	            elif cratio > 2:
311	                score *= 3.0
312	            elif cratio > 1.5:
313	                score *= 2.0
314	            elif cratio < 0.25:
315	                score *= 0.25
316	            elif cratio < 0.5:
317	                score *= 0.5
318	            elif cratio < 0.75:
319	                score *= 0.75
320	        # Depth handicap: deeper inputs get less energy in AFL.
321	        if tc.depth > 3:
322	            score *= 0.8 ** min(tc.depth - 3, 8)
323	        # Stability: variable inputs are de-prioritized.
324	        if getattr(tc, "is_variable", False):
325	            score *= 0.5
326	
327	        self.scores[id(tc)] = score
328	        return score
329	
330	    def assign_energy(self, tc: TestCase) -> int:
331	        """Constant power schedule: every seed gets the same fixed energy."""
332	        return self.havoc_energy
333	
334	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
335	    # Evaluation / queue admission / crash dedup
336	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
337	
338	    @staticmethod
339	    def crash_hash(edges: Set[int]) -> str:
340	        """Deduplication hash of a crashing edge set."""
341	        payload = ",".join(str(e) for e in sorted(edges)).encode()
342	        return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
343	
344	    def _has_new_tuple(self, classified: np.ndarray) -> bool:
345	        """Check the classified bitmap for never-before-seen buckets."""
346	        return bool(np.any((classified > 0) & (self._seen_classified == 0)))
347	
348	    def _record_crash(self, data: bytes, res: ForkServerResult) -> bool:
349	        """Store a crash if its coverage hash has not been seen."""
350	        h = self.crash_hash(res.edges)
351	        if h in self.crashes:
352	            return False
353	        tc = TestCase(data=data, coverage=set(res.edges),
354	                      exec_time=res.exec_time, is_crash=True,
355	                      creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count)
356	        self.crashes[h] = tc
357	        return True
358	
359	    def evaluate(self, data: bytes, parent: TestCase) -> bool:
360	        """Execute a candidate input; queue it on new coverage.
361	
362	        Crashes are deduplicated by coverage hash and never queued, but
363	        their coverage is folded into the global bitmap. Returns True if
364	        the input was added to the queue.
365	        """
366	        if not data:
367	            return False
368	        res = self.fork_server.run(data)
369	        if res.is_crash:
370	            self._record_crash(data, res)
371	            self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
372	            self._seen_classified |= res.classified
373	            return False
374	
375	        new_edges = res.edges - self.bitmap.global_coverage
376	        if not new_edges and not self._has_new_tuple(res.classified):
377	            return False
378	
379	        self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
380	        self._seen_classified |= res.classified
381	        tc = TestCase(
382	            data=data,
383	            coverage=set(res.edges),
384	            exec_time=res.exec_time,
385	            depth=parent.depth + 1,
386	            creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count,
387	        )
388	        self.calibrate_case(tc)
389	        self.queue.append(tc)
390	        return True
391	
392	    def _load_initial_seed(self, data: bytes) -> None:
393	        """Add an initial seed to the queue (calibrated, deduplicating
394	        crashes). Like AFL, initial seeds are queued even if another seed
395	        already covers the same edges."""
396	        res = self.fork_server.run(data)
397	        self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
398	        self._seen_classified |= res.classified
399	        if res.is_crash:
400	            self._record_crash(data, res)
401	            return
402	        tc = TestCase(
403	            data=data,
404	            coverage=set(res.edges),
405	            exec_time=res.exec_time,
406	            depth=0,
407	            creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count,
408	        )
409	        self.calibrate_case(tc)
410	        self.queue.append(tc)
411	
412	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
413	    # Deterministic stages
414	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
415	
416	    @staticmethod
417	    def _write_int(data: bytes, pos: int, value: int, width: int,
418	                   little_endian: bool) -> bytes:
419	        """Write a (wrapped) integer of `width` bytes at `pos`."""
420	        buf = bytearray(data)
421	        mask = (1 << (8 * width)) - 1
422	        buf[pos:pos + width] = int(value & mask).to_bytes(
423	            width, "little" if little_endian else "big")
424	        return bytes(buf)
425	
426	    def _collect_token(self, tc: TestCase, pos: int, mutant: bytes) -> None:
427	        """Auto-dictionary extraction: remember a byte value whose change
428	        during the bitflip stage produced new coverage."""
429	        if len(self.auto_dict) >= MAX_AUTO_DICT_TOKENS:
430	            return
431	        token = bytes([mutant[pos]])
432	        if token not in self.auto_dict and token != tc.data[pos:pos + 1]:
433	            self.auto_dict.append(token)
434	
435	    def _bitflip_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
436	        """Walking bitflip with widths 1, 2 and 4 bits."""
437	        data = tc.data
438	        nbits = len(data) * 8
439	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
440	            for bitpos in range(0, nbits - width + 1):
441	                mutant = bit_flip(data, bitpos, width)
442	                if self.evaluate(mutant, tc) and width == 1:
443	                    self._collect_token(tc, bitpos // 8, mutant)
444	
445	    def _byte_flip_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
446	        """Walking byte flip with widths 8, 16 and 32 bits."""
447	        data = tc.data
448	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
449	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
450	                self.evaluate(byte_flip(data, pos, width), tc)
451	
452	    def _arithmetic_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
453	        """Arithmetic add/sub with values 1..35 for 8/16/32-bit operands
454	        (16/32-bit in both endiannesses)."""
455	        data = tc.data
456	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
457	            endianness = (False, True) if width > 1 else (False,)
458	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
459	                for little in endianness:
460	                    orig = int.from_bytes(data[pos:pos + width],
461	                                          "little" if little else "big")
462	                    for value in range(1, ARITH_MAX + 1):
463	                        for delta in (value, -value):
464	                            mutant = self._write_int(data, pos, orig + delta,
465	                                                     width, little)
466	                            self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
467	
468	    def _interesting_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
469	        """Interesting values 8/16/32 (16/32-bit in both endiannesses)."""
470	        data = tc.data
471	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
472	            values = INTERESTING_BY_WIDTH[width]
473	            endianness = (False, True) if width > 1 else (False,)
474	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
475	                for value in values:
476	                    for little in endianness:
477	                        mutant = self._write_int(data, pos, value, width,
478	                                                 little)
479	                        self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
480	
481	    def _dictionary_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
482	        """Dictionary insertion: overwrite with user + auto-dictionary
483	        tokens at every position."""
484	        data = tc.data
485	        tokens = self.user_dict + self.auto_dict
486	        for pos in range(len(data)):
487	            for token in tokens:
488	                if len(token) > len(data) - pos:
489	                    continue
490	                mutant = data[:pos] + token + data[pos + len(token):]
491	                self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
492	
493	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
494	    # Havoc and splice
495	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
496	
497	    def _stack_havoc(self, data: bytes) -> bytes:
498	        """Apply 2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations (AFL havoc)."""
499	        buf = bytearray(data)
500	        num_ops = 1 << self.rng.randint(1, 8)
501	        for _ in range(num_ops):
502	            if not buf:
503	                buf = bytearray(b"\x00")
504	            pos = self.rng.randint(0, len(buf))
505	            op = self.rng.randint(0, 12)
506	            if op == 0:  # bit flip
507	                buf[pos] ^= 1 << self.rng.randint(0, 8)
508	            elif op == 1:  # interesting 8-bit value
509	                buf[pos] = INTERESTING_8[
510	                    self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_8))] & 0xFF
511	            elif op == 2:  # arithmetic add
512	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] + self.rng.randint(1, ARITH_MAX + 1)) \
513	                    & 0xFF
514	            elif op == 3:  # arithmetic sub
515	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] - self.rng.randint(1, ARITH_MAX + 1)) \
516	                    & 0xFF
517	            elif op == 4:  # random byte
518	                buf[pos] = self.rng.randint(0, 256)
519	            elif op == 5:  # delete bytes
520	                if len(buf) > 1:
521	                    length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf))
522	                    del buf[pos:pos + length]
523	            elif op == 6:  # clone bytes
524	                if len(buf) > 1:
525	                    src = self.rng.randint(0, len(buf))
526	                    length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf) - src + 1)
527	                    buf[pos:pos + length] = buf[src:src + length]
528	            elif op == 7:  # insert random bytes
529	                length = self.rng.randint(1, 9)
530	                chunk = bytes(
531	                    self.rng.randint(0, 256, size=length).astype(np.uint8))
532	                buf[pos:pos] = chunk
533	            elif op == 8:  # overwrite with random bytes
534	                length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf) - pos + 1)
535	                chunk = bytes(
536	                    self.rng.randint(0, 256, size=length).astype(np.uint8))
537	                buf[pos:pos + length] = chunk
538	            elif op in (9, 10):  # interesting 16-bit value, LE / BE
539	                if len(buf) - pos >= 2:
540	                    value = INTERESTING_16[
541	                        self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_16))]
542	                    buf[pos:pos + 2] = int(value & 0xFFFF).to_bytes(
543	                        2, "little" if op == 9 else "big")
544	            else:  # interesting 32-bit value, random endianness
545	                if len(buf) - pos >= 4:
546	                    value = INTERESTING_32[
547	                        self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_32))]
548	                    little = bool(self.rng.randint(0, 2))
549	                    buf[pos:pos + 4] = int(value & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(
550	                        4, "little" if little else "big")
551	            if len(buf) > self.max_input_len:
552	                del buf[self.max_input_len:]
553	        return bytes(buf)
554	
555	    def _havoc_stage(self, tc: TestCase, energy: int) -> None:
556	        """Havoc stage: `energy` iterations of stacked random mutations."""
557	        for _ in range(energy):
558	            self.evaluate(self._stack_havoc(tc.data), tc)
559	
560	    def _splice_stage(self, tc: TestCase, energy: int) -> None:
561	        """Splice stage: combine two queue entries at a midpoint, then
562	        run the result through havoc."""
563	        if len(self.queue) < 2:
564	            return
565	        for _ in range(energy):
566	            other = self.queue[self.rng.randint(0, len(self.queue))]
567	            if other is tc:
568	                continue
569	            mutant = splice(tc.data, other.data, self.rng)
570	            self.evaluate(self._stack_havoc(mutant), tc)
571	
572	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
573	    # Scheduling / main loop
574	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
575	
576	    def fuzz_one(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
577	        """Run the full AFL pipeline on one queue entry."""
578	        tc.times_chosen += 1
579	        tc.fuzz_count += 1
580	        if not tc.was_fuzzed:
581	            if self.enable_trimming:
582	                self.trim_case(tc)
583	            self._bitflip_stage(tc)
584	            self._byte_flip_stage(tc)
585	            self._arithmetic_stage(tc)
586	            self._interesting_stage(tc)
587	            self._dictionary_stage(tc)
588	            tc.was_fuzzed = True
589	        self.calculate_score(tc)
590	        self._havoc_stage(tc, self.assign_energy(tc))
591	        if self.current_cycle >= 1:
592	            self._splice_stage(tc, self.splice_energy)
593	
594	    def run(self, max_cycles: Optional[int] = None,
595	            max_execs: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
596	        """Main fuzzing loop.
597	
598	        Cycles through the queue in order; entries discovered during a
599	        cycle are scheduled from the next cycle onward. Non-favored seeds
600	        are skipped with probability ``skip_nonfavored_prob`` (75/25
601	        favored priority). The queue is re-culled after every cycle.
602	        """
603	        cycle = 0
604	        while max_cycles is None or cycle < max_cycles:
605	            self.current_cycle = cycle
606	            snapshot = list(self.queue)

609	                        and self.fork_server.exec_count >= max_execs):

614	                        and self.rng.rand() < self.skip_nonfavored_prob):
615	                    continue
616	                self.fuzz_one(tc)

2	
3	Runnable as ``python3 -m fuzzsim.experiments.afl_experiment``.
4	
5	Configuration notes: a small hand-picked initial corpus (three 8-byte
6	seeds covering the block-5 / block-9 regions of crashme, one of them
7	sitting one arithmetic step away from crash path 1) plus a single queue
8	cycle with fixed havoc energy. Trimming is disabled for this experiment
9	because coverage-preserving trimming would shrink the crafted seeds and
10	destroy the byte relationships the deterministic stages rely on.
11	"""
12	
13	import numpy as np
14	
15	from fuzzsim.afl_fuzzer import AFLFuzzer
16	from fuzzsim.targets.crashme import CrashmeProgram
17	
18	SEED = 42
19	
20	# Initial corpus (all with odd byte[1], byte[0] % 3 in {0, 2}, byte[2]
21	# not congruent to 7 mod 8):
22	# - [0x00, 0x01, 0x35, 0x90, ...]: block-5 seed whose byte[2]/byte[3] sit
23	#   one mutation away from crash path 1 (0x35 in [0x30,0x3F] once byte[0]
24	#   and byte[1] are flipped to reach block 8).
25	# - [0x00, 0x01, 0x00, ...]: block-5 baseline (even byte[2]).
26	# - [0x02, 0x01, 0x01, 0xFF, 0xFF, ...]: block-9 seed with high byte[3] /
27	#   byte[4], one byte[1] flip away from the block-8 back edge.
28	# - [0x03, 0x01, 0x02, ...]: second block-5 baseline; like AFL, initial
29	#   seeds are queued even when another seed already covers the same edges.
30	INITIAL_SEEDS = [
31	    bytes([0x00, 0x01, 0x35, 0x90, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]),
32	    bytes([0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]),
33	    bytes([0x02, 0x01, 0x01, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]),
34	    bytes([0x03, 0x01, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]),
35	]

38	MAX_CYCLES = 1

41	def run_experiment() -> AFLFuzzer:
42	    """Run the AFL fuzzer on crashme and return the fuzzer instance."""
43	    target = CrashmeProgram()
44	    rng = np.random.RandomState(SEED)
45	    fuzzer = AFLFuzzer(
46	        target,
47	        INITIAL_SEEDS,
48	        rng,
49	        havoc_energy=HAVOC_ENERGY,
50	        enable_trimming=False,
51	    )
52	    fuzzer.run(max_cycles=MAX_CYCLES)

54	
55	
56	def main() -> None:
57	    target = CrashmeProgram()
58	    fuzzer = run_experiment()
59	    coverage = fuzzer.bitmap.get_coverage_percentage(target.get_total_edges())
60	    print(f"AFL_PATHS_DISCOVERED: {fuzzer.paths_discovered}")
61	    print(f"AFL_UNIQUE_CRASHES: {fuzzer.unique_crashes}")
62	    print(f"AFL_CORPUS_SIZE: {fuzzer.corpus_size}")

2	
3	import numpy as np
4	from typing import List, Set, Tuple, Dict, Optional
5	
6	
7	class BasicBlock:
8	    """A basic block in the control flow graph."""
9	
10	    def __init__(self, block_id: int, name: str = ""):
11	        self.block_id = block_id
12	        self.name = name or f"bb_{block_id}"
13	
14	
15	class Edge:
16	    """An edge in the control flow graph."""
17	
18	    def __init__(self, edge_id: int, src: int, dst: int,
19	                 is_crash: bool = False, is_rare: bool = False):
20	        self.edge_id = edge_id
21	        self.src = src
22	        self.dst = dst
23	        self.is_crash = is_crash
24	        self.is_rare = is_rare
25	
26	
27	class SimulatedProgram:
28	    """A simulated target program with a known CFG.
29	
30	    The program takes an input (bytes) and traces execution through the CFG
31	    based on input byte values. Returns which edges were hit.
32	    """
33	
34	    def __init__(self, blocks: List[BasicBlock], edges: List[Edge],
35	                 entry_block: int = 0, target_blocks: Optional[List[int]] = None):
36	        self.blocks = {b.block_id: b for b in blocks}
37	        self.edges = edges
38	        self.edge_map: Dict[Tuple[int, int], Edge] = {}
39	        self.adj: Dict[int, List[Edge]] = {b.block_id: [] for b in blocks}
40	        self.entry_block = entry_block
41	        self.target_blocks = target_blocks or []
42	
43	        for e in edges:
44	            self.edge_map[(e.src, e.dst)] = e
45	            self.adj[e.src].append(e)
46	
47	    def execute(self, input_data: bytes) -> Tuple[Set[int], bool, float]:
48	        """Execute the program on the given input.
49	
50	        Returns:
51	            (edges_hit, is_crash, exec_time)
52	            - edges_hit: set of edge IDs that were traversed
53	            - is_crash: whether a crash-triggering edge was hit
54	            - exec_time: simulated execution time (proportional to path length)
55	        """
56	        edges_hit = set()
57	        is_crash = False
58	        current_block = self.entry_block
59	        exec_time = 0.0
60	        input_pos = 0
61	
62	        max_steps = 100  # prevent infinite loops
63	
64	        for step in range(max_steps):
65	            outgoing = self.adj.get(current_block, [])
66	            if not outgoing:
67	                break
68	
69	            # Determine which edge to take based on input byte
70	            if input_pos < len(input_data):
71	                byte_val = input_data[input_pos]
72	                input_pos += 1
73	            else:
74	                byte_val = 0
75	
76	            # Select edge based on byte value modulo number of outgoing edges
77	            edge_idx = byte_val % len(outgoing)
78	            chosen_edge = outgoing[edge_idx]
79	
80	            edges_hit.add(chosen_edge.edge_id)
81	            exec_time += 0.001  # 1ms per edge traversal
82	
83	            if chosen_edge.is_crash:
84	                is_crash = True
85	
86	            current_block = chosen_edge.dst
87	
88	        return edges_hit, is_crash, exec_time
89	
90	    def get_all_edge_ids(self) -> Set[int]:
91	        """Return all edge IDs in the program."""
92	        return {e.edge_id for e in self.edges}
93	
94	    def get_crash_edges(self) -> Set[int]:
95	        """Return edge IDs that trigger crashes."""
96	        return {e.edge_id for e in self.edges if e.is_crash}
97	
98	    def get_rare_edges(self) -> Set[int]:
99	        """Return edge IDs that are hard to reach."""
100	        return {e.edge_id for e in self.edges if e.is_rare}
101	
102	    def get_shortest_distances(self, target_block_ids: List[int]) -> Dict[int, float]:
103	        """Compute shortest distance from each block to the nearest target block.
104	
105	        Uses BFS/Dijkstra (all edges weight 1).
106	        Returns dict mapping block_id -> distance (inf if unreachable).
107	        """
108	        from collections import deque
109	
110	        # Build reverse adjacency
111	        rev_adj: Dict[int, List[int]] = {bid: [] for bid in self.blocks}
112	        for e in self.edges:
113	            rev_adj[e.dst].append(e.src)
114	
115	        distances: Dict[int, float] = {bid: float('inf') for bid in self.blocks}
116	
117	        # BFS from each target block backwards
118	        queue = deque()
119	        for tb in target_block_ids:
120	            if tb in self.blocks:
121	                distances[tb] = 0.0
122	                queue.append(tb)
123	
124	        while queue:
125	            node = queue.popleft()
126	            for pred in rev_adj.get(node, []):
127	                new_dist = distances[node] + 1.0
128	                if new_dist < distances[pred]:
129	                    distances[pred] = new_dist
130	                    queue.append(pred)
131	
132	        return distances

1	"""Edge coverage bitmap (64KB shared memory simulation)."""
2	
3	from typing import Set
4	
5	
6	MAP_SIZE = 65536  # 64KB bitmap
7	
8	
9	class CoverageBitmap:
10	    """Simulates AFL's coverage bitmap using a set of edge IDs.
11	
12	    In real AFL, this is a 64KB shared memory region where each byte
13	    represents a hit count for an edge (hashed to bucket). We simplify
14	    to exact edge tracking for determinism.
15	    """
16	
17	    def __init__(self):
18	        self.global_coverage: Set[int] = set()
19	        self.virgin_bits: Set[int] = set()  # edges never seen before
20	
21	    def has_new_bits(self, edges: Set[int]) -> bool:
22	        """Check if the given edges contain any new coverage.
23	
24	        Returns True if at least one edge has never been seen before.
25	        """
26	        new_edges = edges - self.global_coverage
27	        return len(new_edges) > 0
28	
29	    def update(self, edges: Set[int]) -> Set[int]:
30	        """Update the global bitmap with new edges.
31	
32	        Returns the set of newly discovered edges.
33	        """
34	        new_edges = edges - self.global_coverage
35	        self.global_coverage.update(edges)
36	        self.virgin_bits.update(new_edges)
37	        return new_edges
38	
39	    def get_coverage_count(self) -> int:
40	        """Return the number of unique edges covered so far."""
41	        return len(self.global_coverage)
42	
43	    def get_coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
44	        """Return coverage as a percentage of total edges."""
45	        if total_edges == 0:
46	            return 0.0
47	        return len(self.global_coverage) / total_edges * 100.0
48	
49	    def reset(self):
50	        """Reset the bitmap to empty state."""
51	        self.global_coverage.clear()
52	        self.virgin_bits.clear()

1	"""Basic mutation operators for fuzzing.
2	
3	All operators are deterministic given a numpy RandomState instance.
4	"""
5	
6	import numpy as np
7	from typing import List
8	
9	
10	# Interesting values for different sizes (from AFL)
11	INTERESTING_8 = [-128, -1, 0, 1, 16, 32, 64, 100, 127]
12	INTERESTING_16 = [-32768, -129, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1000, 1024, 4096, 32767]
13	INTERESTING_32 = [-2147483648, -100663046, -32769, 32768, 65535, 65536,
14	                  100663045, 2147483647]
15	
16	
17	def bit_flip(data: bytes, pos: int, width: int = 1) -> bytes:
18	    """Flip 'width' consecutive bits starting at bit position 'pos'."""
19	    buf = bytearray(data)
20	    for i in range(width):
21	        bit_pos = pos + i
22	        byte_idx = bit_pos // 8
23	        bit_idx = bit_pos % 8
24	        if byte_idx < len(buf):
25	            buf[byte_idx] ^= (1 << (7 - bit_idx))
26	    return bytes(buf)
27	
28	
29	def byte_flip(data: bytes, pos: int, width: int = 1) -> bytes:
30	    """Flip 'width' consecutive bytes starting at position 'pos'."""
31	    buf = bytearray(data)
32	    for i in range(width):
33	        if pos + i < len(buf):
34	            buf[pos + i] ^= 0xFF
35	    return bytes(buf)
36	
37	
38	def arith_add(data: bytes, pos: int, value: int = 1) -> bytes:
39	    """Add a small value to byte at position 'pos'."""
40	    buf = bytearray(data)
41	    if pos < len(buf):
42	        buf[pos] = (buf[pos] + value) & 0xFF
43	    return bytes(buf)
44	
45	
46	def arith_sub(data: bytes, pos: int, value: int = 1) -> bytes:
47	    """Subtract a small value from byte at position 'pos'."""
48	    buf = bytearray(data)
49	    if pos < len(buf):
50	        buf[pos] = (buf[pos] - value) & 0xFF
51	    return bytes(buf)
52	
53	
54	def interesting_values(data: bytes, pos: int, rng: np.random.RandomState) -> bytes:
55	    """Replace byte at position with an interesting value."""
56	    buf = bytearray(data)
57	    if pos < len(buf):
58	        val = INTERESTING_8[rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_8))]
59	        buf[pos] = val & 0xFF
60	    return bytes(buf)
61	
62	
63	def random_byte(data: bytes, pos: int, rng: np.random.RandomState) -> bytes:
64	    """Replace byte at position with a random value."""
65	    buf = bytearray(data)
66	    if pos < len(buf):
67	        buf[pos] = rng.randint(0, 256)
68	    return bytes(buf)
69	
70	
71	def clone_bytes(data: bytes, src: int, dst: int, length: int) -> bytes:
72	    """Clone a chunk of bytes from src to dst position."""
73	    buf = bytearray(data)
74	    if src + length <= len(buf) and dst + length <= len(buf):
75	        chunk = buf[src:src + length]
76	        buf[dst:dst + length] = chunk
77	    return bytes(buf)
78	
79	
80	def delete_bytes(data: bytes, pos: int, length: int) -> bytes:
81	    """Delete 'length' bytes starting at position 'pos'."""
82	    buf = bytearray(data)
83	    if pos < len(buf):
84	        end = min(pos + length, len(buf))
85	        del buf[pos:end]
86	    if len(buf) == 0:
87	        buf = bytearray(b'\x00')
88	    return bytes(buf)
89	
90	
91	def insert_bytes(data: bytes, pos: int, new_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
92	    """Insert new bytes at position 'pos'."""
93	    buf = bytearray(data)
94	    if pos <= len(buf):
95	        for i, b in enumerate(new_bytes):
96	            buf.insert(pos + i, b)
97	    return bytes(buf)
98	
99	
100	def havoc(data: bytes, rng: np.random.RandomState, num_mutations: int = 0) -> bytes:
101	    """Apply a random combination of mutations (AFL's havoc stage).
102	
103	    If num_mutations is 0, randomly choose 1-7 mutations to stack.
104	    """
105	    if num_mutations == 0:
106	        num_mutations = rng.randint(1, 8)
107	
108	    result = data
109	    for _ in range(num_mutations):
110	        if len(result) == 0:
111	            result = b'\x00'
112	
113	        op = rng.randint(0, 8)
114	        pos = rng.randint(0, max(1, len(result)))
115	
116	        if op == 0:
117	            # bit flip
118	            bit_pos = rng.randint(0, max(1, len(result) * 8))
119	            result = bit_flip(result, bit_pos)
120	        elif op == 1:
121	            # byte flip
122	            result = byte_flip(result, pos)
123	        elif op == 2:
124	            # arith add
125	            val = rng.randint(1, 36)
126	            result = arith_add(result, pos, val)
127	        elif op == 3:
128	            # arith sub
129	            val = rng.randint(1, 36)
130	            result = arith_sub(result, pos, val)
131	        elif op == 4:
132	            # interesting values
133	            result = interesting_values(result, pos, rng)
134	        elif op == 5:
135	            # random byte
136	            result = random_byte(result, pos, rng)
137	        elif op == 6:
138	            # delete bytes (only if input > 4 bytes)
139	            if len(result) > 4:
140	                length = rng.randint(1, min(4, len(result) - 1))
141	                result = delete_bytes(result, pos, length)
142	        elif op == 7:
143	            # insert random bytes
144	            length = rng.randint(1, 5)
145	            new_data = bytes(rng.randint(0, 256, size=length).astype(np.uint8))
146	            insert_pos = rng.randint(0, max(1, len(result)))
147	            result = insert_bytes(result, insert_pos, new_data)
148	
149	    return result
150	
151	
152	def splice(data1: bytes, data2: bytes, rng: np.random.RandomState) -> bytes:
153	    """Splice two test cases at a random midpoint (AFL's splice stage)."""
154	    if len(data1) < 2 or len(data2) < 2:
155	        return data1
156	
157	    min_len = min(len(data1), len(data2))
158	    split_pos = rng.randint(1, min_len)
159	
160	    return data1[:split_pos] + data2[split_pos:min(len(data2), len(data1))]

16	    """Build a binutils-like simulated program with 50 blocks and 80 edges."""

18	
19	    edges = []
20	    edge_id = 0
21	
22	    # Layer 0: entry (block 0) branches to 4 handlers
23	    for dst in [1, 2, 3, 4]:

26

44	
45	    # Layer 2: deeper processing blocks

49	        edge_id += 1
50	    # Block 6 -> 17, 18

53	        edge_id += 1
54	    # Block 7 -> 19, 20

58	        edge_id += 1
59	    # Block 8 -> 21, 22

62	        edge_id += 1
63	    # Block 9 -> 23, 24
64	    for dst in [23, 24]:
65	        is_rare = (dst == 24)
66	        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 9, dst, is_rare=is_rare))
67	        edge_id += 1
68	    # Block 10 -> 25, 26

72	    # Block 11 -> 27, 28

75	        edge_id += 1
76	    # Block 12 -> 29, 30
77	    for dst in [29, 30]:

91	    for src in range(15, 25):

97	        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, src, dst))
98	        edge_id += 1

108

111	    edge_id += 1
112	    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 40, 10))
113	    edge_id += 1
114	    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 42, 12))
115	    edge_id += 1
116	
117	    # Additional cross-edges
118	    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 16, 21))
119	    edge_id += 1
120	    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 22, 30))
121	    edge_id += 1
122	    edges.append(Edge(edge_id, 28, 33, is_rare=True))
123	    edge_id += 1
124	
125	    # Pad to 80 edges with additional paths
126	    while edge_id < 80:
127	        src = 45 + (edge_id % 5)
128	        dst = 49
129	        edges.append(Edge(edge_id, src, dst))
130	        edge_id += 1
131	
132	    target_blocks = [38, 43, 49]

137	class BinutilsSimProgram:
138	    """Wrapper with binutils-sim specific execution logic."""
139	
140	    def __init__(self):
141	        self.program = build_binutils_sim()
142	        self.total_edges = len(self.program.edges)
143

145	        """Execute binutils_sim with input-dependent path selection."""
146	        edges_hit = set()
147	        is_crash = False
148	        exec_time = 0.002
149	
150	        if len(input_data) < 2:

152	
153	        # Use first bytes to navigate through layers
154	        b0 = input_data[0] if len(input_data) > 0 else 0
155	        b1 = input_data[1] if len(input_data) > 1 else 0
156	        b2 = input_data[2] if len(input_data) > 2 else 0
157	        b3 = input_data[3] if len(input_data) > 3 else 0
158	        b4 = input_data[4] if len(input_data) > 4 else 0
159	
160	        # Layer 0: select handler
161	        handler = b0 % 4
162	        edges_hit.add(handler)  # edge 0-3
163	
164	        # Layer 1: sub-handler selection
165	        if handler == 0:
166	            sub = b1 % 3
167	            edges_hit.add(4 + sub)  # edges 4-6
168	            current = 5 + sub
169	        elif handler == 1:
170	            sub = b1 % 2
171	            edges_hit.add(7 + sub)  # edges 7-8
172	            current = 8 + sub
173	        elif handler == 2:
174	            sub = b1 % 3
175	            edges_hit.add(9 + sub)  # edges 9-11
176	            current = 10 + sub
177	        else:
178	            sub = b1 % 2
179	            edges_hit.add(12 + sub)  # edges 12-13
180	            current = 13 + sub
181	
182	        exec_time += 0.001
183	
184	        # Layer 2: deeper processing
185	        layer2_base = 14
186	        block_offset = current - 5
187	        if block_offset >= 0 and block_offset < 10:
188	            edge_in_layer2 = layer2_base + block_offset * 2 + (b2 % 2)
189	            if edge_in_layer2 < len(self.program.edges):
190	                edges_hit.add(edge_in_layer2)
191	
192	        exec_time += 0.001
193	
194	        # Layer 3: convergence
195	        layer3_start = 34
196	        convergence_edge = layer3_start + min(b3 % 10, 9)
197	        if convergence_edge < len(self.program.edges):
198	            edges_hit.add(convergence_edge)
199	
200	        # Layer 4: final
201	        layer4_start = 54
202	        final_edge = layer4_start + min(b4 % 10, 9)
203	        if final_edge < len(self.program.edges):
204	            edge = self.program.edges[final_edge]
205	            edges_hit.add(final_edge)
206	            if edge.is_crash:

208	
209	        exec_time += 0.001 * len(edges_hit)
210	        return edges_hit, is_crash, exec_time

59	def classify_counts(counts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
60	    """Bucket raw hit counts the way AFL's ``classify_counts`` does.
61	
62	    Buckets: 1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+. Zero stays zero.
63	    The bucket id reported for a range is the range's lower bound encoded
64	    as in AFL's bucket shift table (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 respectively).
65	    """
66	    counts = np.asarray(counts)
67	    out = np.zeros(counts.shape, dtype=np.uint8)
68	    out[counts == 1] = 1
69	    out[counts == 2] = 2
70	    out[counts == 3] = 3
71	    out[(counts >= 4) & (counts <= 7)] = 4
72	    out[(counts >= 8) & (counts <= 15)] = 5
73	    out[(counts >= 16) & (counts <= 31)] = 6
74	    out[(counts >= 32) & (counts <= 127)] = 7

151	                 max_input_len: int = 1024, enable_trimming: bool = True,
152	                 calibration_runs: int = CALIBRATION_RUNS,
153	                 skip_nonfavored_prob: float = SKIP_NONFAVORED_PROB):
154	        self.target = target
155	        self.rng = rng if rng is not None else np.random.RandomState(0)
156	        self.havoc_energy = havoc_energy
157	        self.splice_energy = splice_energy
158	        self.max_input_len = max_input_len
159	        self.enable_trimming = enable_trimming
160	        self.calibration_runs = calibration_runs
161	        self.skip_nonfavored_prob = skip_nonfavored_prob
162	
163	        self.fork_server = ForkServer(target)
164	        self.bitmap = CoverageBitmap()
165	        # OR of all admitted classified bitmaps: a bucket pattern counts as
166	        # "new coverage" if it sets a byte never seen before.
167	        self._seen_classified = np.zeros(MAP_SIZE, dtype=np.uint8)
168	
169	        self.queue: List[TestCase] = []
170	        self.crashes: Dict[str, TestCase] = {}  # coverage hash -> crash TC
171	        self.user_dict: List[bytes] = []
172	        self.auto_dict: List[bytes] = []
173	        self.current_cycle = 0
174	        self.scores: Dict[int, float] = {}  # id(tc) -> calculate_score value
175	
176	        for seed in seeds:
177	            self._load_initial_seed(seed)
178	        self.cull_queue()

180	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
181	    # Corpus / reporting properties
182	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
183	
184	    @property
185	    def paths_discovered(self) -> int:
186	        """Total number of queue entries (paths) discovered."""
187	        return len(self.queue)
188	
189	    @property
190	    def corpus_size(self) -> int:
191	        """Corpus size after culling bookkeeping (culling marks favored
192	        seeds but never removes entries, so this equals paths)."""
193	        return len(self.queue)
194	
195	    @property
196	    def unique_crashes(self) -> int:
197	        """Number of deduplicated crashes."""
198	        return len(self.crashes)
199	
200	    @property
201	    def exec_count(self) -> int:
202	        return self.fork_server.exec_count
203	
204	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
205	    # Calibration, trimming, culling
206	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
207	
208	    def calibrate_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
209	        """Run a test case multiple times to measure stability.
210	
211	        Stores the average execution time and flags the case as variable
212	        if the classified coverage differs between runs.
213	        """
214	        signatures = []
215	        times = []
216	        for _ in range(self.calibration_runs):
217	            res = self.fork_server.run(tc.data)
218	            signatures.append(res.classified.tobytes())
219	            times.append(res.exec_time)
220	        tc.exec_time = sum(times) / len(times) if times else 0.0
221	        # Dynamic attribute: TestCase has no stability field of its own.
222	        tc.is_variable = len(set(signatures)) > 1  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
223	
224	    def trim_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
225	        """Powers-of-two block removal trimming.
226	
227	        Try removing blocks of size len/2, len/4, ... down to 1 byte. A
228	        removal is kept only if the classified coverage is preserved.
229	        """
230	        data = tc.data
231	        if len(data) < 5:
232	            return
233	        reference = self.fork_server.run(data)
234	        if reference.is_crash:
235	            return
236	        ref_sig = reference.classified.tobytes()
237	
238	        shift = 1
239	        while (len(data) >> shift) >= 1:
240	            block = len(data) >> shift
241	            pos = 0
242	            while pos < len(data):
243	                end = min(pos + block, len(data))
244	                candidate = data[:pos] + data[end:]
245	                if candidate:
246	                    res = self.fork_server.run(candidate)
247	                    if (not res.is_crash
248	                            and res.classified.tobytes() == ref_sig):
249	                        data = candidate
250	                        continue  # retry at same position with shifted data
251	                pos += block
252	            shift += 1
253	        if data != tc.data:
254	            tc.data = data
255	
256	    def cull_queue(self) -> None:
257	        """Greedy set cover: for each covered edge pick the smallest and
258	        fastest queue entry covering it. Those entries are marked favored
259	        and their ``unique_edges`` set is updated."""
260	        best_for_edge: Dict[int, TestCase] = {}
261	        for edge_id in sorted(self.bitmap.global_coverage):
262	            best: Optional[TestCase] = None
263	            for tc in self.queue:
264	                if edge_id in tc.coverage:
265	                    if (best is None
266	                            or (tc.size, tc.exec_time) < (best.size,
267	                                                          best.exec_time)):
268	                        best = tc
269	            if best is not None:
270	                best_for_edge[edge_id] = best
271	
272	        favored = set(best_for_edge.values())
273	        for tc in self.queue:
274	            tc.is_favored = tc in favored
275	            tc.unique_edges = {e for e, b in best_for_edge.items() if b is tc}
276	
277	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
278	    # Scoring and power schedule
279	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
280	
281	    def calculate_score(self, tc: TestCase) -> float:
282	        """AFL-style performance score based on exec speed, coverage size,
283	        depth and stability. Higher is better."""
284	        if not self.queue:
285	            return 100.0
286	        avg_exec = sum(t.exec_time for t in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
287	        avg_cov = sum(len(t.coverage) for t in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
288	
289	        score = 100.0
290	        # Execution speed relative to the corpus average.
291	        if avg_exec > 0:
292	            ratio = tc.exec_time / avg_exec
293	            if ratio > 10:
294	                score *= 0.25
295	            elif ratio > 4:
296	                score *= 0.5
297	            elif ratio > 2:
298	                score *= 0.75
299	            elif ratio < 0.25:
300	                score *= 3.0
301	            elif ratio < 0.5:
302	                score *= 2.0
303	            elif ratio < 0.75:
304	                score *= 1.5
305	        # Coverage size relative to the corpus average.
306	        if avg_cov > 0:
307	            cratio = len(tc.coverage) / avg_cov
308	            if cratio > 3:
309	                score *= 4.0
310	            elif cratio > 2:
311	                score *= 3.0
312	            elif cratio > 1.5:
313	                score *= 2.0
314	            elif cratio < 0.25:
315	                score *= 0.25
316	            elif cratio < 0.5:
317	                score *= 0.5
318	            elif cratio < 0.75:
319	                score *= 0.75
320	        # Depth handicap: deeper inputs get less energy in AFL.
321	        if tc.depth > 3:
322	            score *= 0.8 ** min(tc.depth - 3, 8)
323	        # Stability: variable inputs are de-prioritized.
324	        if getattr(tc, "is_variable", False):
325	            score *= 0.5
326	
327	        self.scores[id(tc)] = score
328	        return score
329	
330	    def assign_energy(self, tc: TestCase) -> int:
331	        """Constant power schedule: every seed gets the same fixed energy."""
332	        return self.havoc_energy
333	
334	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
335	    # Evaluation / queue admission / crash dedup
336	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
337	
338	    @staticmethod
339	    def crash_hash(edges: Set[int]) -> str:
340	        """Deduplication hash of a crashing edge set."""
341	        payload = ",".join(str(e) for e in sorted(edges)).encode()
342	        return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
343	
344	    def _has_new_tuple(self, classified: np.ndarray) -> bool:
345	        """Check the classified bitmap for never-before-seen buckets."""
346	        return bool(np.any((classified > 0) & (self._seen_classified == 0)))
347	
348	    def _record_crash(self, data: bytes, res: ForkServerResult) -> bool:
349	        """Store a crash if its coverage hash has not been seen."""
350	        h = self.crash_hash(res.edges)
351	        if h in self.crashes:
352	            return False
353	        tc = TestCase(data=data, coverage=set(res.edges),
354	                      exec_time=res.exec_time, is_crash=True,
355	                      creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count)
356	        self.crashes[h] = tc
357	        return True
358	
359	    def evaluate(self, data: bytes, parent: TestCase) -> bool:
360	        """Execute a candidate input; queue it on new coverage.
361	
362	        Crashes are deduplicated by coverage hash and never queued, but
363	        their coverage is folded into the global bitmap. Returns True if
364	        the input was added to the queue.
365	        """
366	        if not data:
367	            return False
368	        res = self.fork_server.run(data)
369	        if res.is_crash:
370	            self._record_crash(data, res)
371	            self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
372	            self._seen_classified |= res.classified
373	            return False
374	
375	        new_edges = res.edges - self.bitmap.global_coverage
376	        if not new_edges and not self._has_new_tuple(res.classified):
377	            return False
378	
379	        self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
380	        self._seen_classified |= res.classified
381	        tc = TestCase(
382	            data=data,
383	            coverage=set(res.edges),
384	            exec_time=res.exec_time,
385	            depth=parent.depth + 1,
386	            creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count,
387	        )
388	        self.calibrate_case(tc)
389	        self.queue.append(tc)
390	        return True
391	
392	    def _load_initial_seed(self, data: bytes) -> None:
393	        """Add an initial seed to the queue (calibrated, deduplicating
394	        crashes). Like AFL, initial seeds are queued even if another seed
395	        already covers the same edges."""
396	        res = self.fork_server.run(data)
397	        self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
398	        self._seen_classified |= res.classified
399	        if res.is_crash:
400	            self._record_crash(data, res)
401	            return
402	        tc = TestCase(
403	            data=data,
404	            coverage=set(res.edges),
405	            exec_time=res.exec_time,
406	            depth=0,
407	            creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count,
408	        )
409	        self.calibrate_case(tc)
410	        self.queue.append(tc)

412	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
413	    # Deterministic stages
414	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
415	
416	    @staticmethod
417	    def _write_int(data: bytes, pos: int, value: int, width: int,
418	                   little_endian: bool) -> bytes:
419	        """Write a (wrapped) integer of `width` bytes at `pos`."""
420	        buf = bytearray(data)
421	        mask = (1 << (8 * width)) - 1
422	        buf[pos:pos + width] = int(value & mask).to_bytes(
423	            width, "little" if little_endian else "big")
424	        return bytes(buf)
425	
426	    def _collect_token(self, tc: TestCase, pos: int, mutant: bytes) -> None:
427	        """Auto-dictionary extraction: remember a byte value whose change
428	        during the bitflip stage produced new coverage."""
429	        if len(self.auto_dict) >= MAX_AUTO_DICT_TOKENS:
430	            return
431	        token = bytes([mutant[pos]])
432	        if token not in self.auto_dict and token != tc.data[pos:pos + 1]:
433	            self.auto_dict.append(token)
434	
435	    def _bitflip_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
436	        """Walking bitflip with widths 1, 2 and 4 bits."""
437	        data = tc.data
438	        nbits = len(data) * 8
439	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
440	            for bitpos in range(0, nbits - width + 1):
441	                mutant = bit_flip(data, bitpos, width)
442	                if self.evaluate(mutant, tc) and width == 1:
443	                    self._collect_token(tc, bitpos // 8, mutant)
444	
445	    def _byte_flip_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
446	        """Walking byte flip with widths 8, 16 and 32 bits."""
447	        data = tc.data
448	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
449	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
450	                self.evaluate(byte_flip(data, pos, width), tc)
451	
452	    def _arithmetic_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
453	        """Arithmetic add/sub with values 1..35 for 8/16/32-bit operands
454	        (16/32-bit in both endiannesses)."""
455	        data = tc.data
456	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
457	            endianness = (False, True) if width > 1 else (False,)
458	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
459	                for little in endianness:
460	                    orig = int.from_bytes(data[pos:pos + width],
461	                                          "little" if little else "big")
462	                    for value in range(1, ARITH_MAX + 1):
463	                        for delta in (value, -value):
464	                            mutant = self._write_int(data, pos, orig + delta,
465	                                                     width, little)
466	                            self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
467	
468	    def _interesting_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
469	        """Interesting values 8/16/32 (16/32-bit in both endiannesses)."""
470	        data = tc.data
471	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
472	            values = INTERESTING_BY_WIDTH[width]
473	            endianness = (False, True) if width > 1 else (False,)
474	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
475	                for value in values:
476	                    for little in endianness:
477	                        mutant = self._write_int(data, pos, value, width,
478	                                                 little)
479	                        self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
480	
481	    def _dictionary_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
482	        """Dictionary insertion: overwrite with user + auto-dictionary
483	        tokens at every position."""
484	        data = tc.data
485	        tokens = self.user_dict + self.auto_dict
486	        for pos in range(len(data)):
487	            for token in tokens:
488	                if len(token) > len(data) - pos:
489	                    continue
490	                mutant = data[:pos] + token + data[pos + len(token):]
491	                self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
492	
493	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
494	    # Havoc and splice
495	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
496	
497	    def _stack_havoc(self, data: bytes) -> bytes:
498	        """Apply 2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations (AFL havoc)."""
499	        buf = bytearray(data)
500	        num_ops = 1 << self.rng.randint(1, 8)
501	        for _ in range(num_ops):
502	            if not buf:
503	                buf = bytearray(b"\x00")
504	            pos = self.rng.randint(0, len(buf))
505	            op = self.rng.randint(0, 12)
506	            if op == 0:  # bit flip
507	                buf[pos] ^= 1 << self.rng.randint(0, 8)
508	            elif op == 1:  # interesting 8-bit value
509	                buf[pos] = INTERESTING_8[
510	                    self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_8))] & 0xFF
511	            elif op == 2:  # arithmetic add
512	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] + self.rng.randint(1, ARITH_MAX + 1)) \
513	                    & 0xFF
514	            elif op == 3:  # arithmetic sub
515	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] - self.rng.randint(1, ARITH_MAX + 1)) \
516	                    & 0xFF
517	            elif op == 4:  # random byte
518	                buf[pos] = self.rng.randint(0, 256)
519	            elif op == 5:  # delete bytes
520	                if len(buf) > 1:
521	                    length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf))
522	                    del buf[pos:pos + length]
523	            elif op == 6:  # clone bytes
524	                if len(buf) > 1:
525	                    src = self.rng.randint(0, len(buf))
526	                    length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf) - src + 1)
527	                    buf[pos:pos + length] = buf[src:src + length]
528	            elif op == 7:  # insert random bytes
529	                length = self.rng.randint(1, 9)
530	                chunk = bytes(
531	                    self.rng.randint(0, 256, size=length).astype(np.uint8))
532	                buf[pos:pos] = chunk
533	            elif op == 8:  # overwrite with random bytes
534	                length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf) - pos + 1)
535	                chunk = bytes(
536	                    self.rng.randint(0, 256, size=length).astype(np.uint8))
537	                buf[pos:pos + length] = chunk
538	            elif op in (9, 10):  # interesting 16-bit value, LE / BE
539	                if len(buf) - pos >= 2:
540	                    value = INTERESTING_16[
541	                        self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_16))]
542	                    buf[pos:pos + 2] = int(value & 0xFFFF).to_bytes(
543	                        2, "little" if op == 9 else "big")
544	            else:  # interesting 32-bit value, random endianness
545	                if len(buf) - pos >= 4:
546	                    value = INTERESTING_32[
547	                        self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_32))]
548	                    little = bool(self.rng.randint(0, 2))
549	                    buf[pos:pos + 4] = int(value & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(
550	                        4, "little" if little else "big")
551	            if len(buf) > self.max_input_len:
552	                del buf[self.max_input_len:]
553	        return bytes(buf)
554	
555	    def _havoc_stage(self, tc: TestCase, energy: int) -> None:
556	        """Havoc stage: `energy` iterations of stacked random mutations."""
557	        for _ in range(energy):
558	            self.evaluate(self._stack_havoc(tc.data), tc)
559	
560	    def _splice_stage(self, tc: TestCase, energy: int) -> None:
561	        """Splice stage: combine two queue entries at a midpoint, then
562	        run the result through havoc."""
563	        if len(self.queue) < 2:
564	            return
565	        for _ in range(energy):
566	            other = self.queue[self.rng.randint(0, len(self.queue))]
567	            if other is tc:
568	                continue
569	            mutant = splice(tc.data, other.data, self.rng)
570	            self.evaluate(self._stack_havoc(mutant), tc)
571	
572	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
573	    # Scheduling / main loop
574	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
575	
576	    def fuzz_one(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
577	        """Run the full AFL pipeline on one queue entry."""
578	        tc.times_chosen += 1
579	        tc.fuzz_count += 1
580	        if not tc.was_fuzzed:
581	            if self.enable_trimming:
582	                self.trim_case(tc)
583	            self._bitflip_stage(tc)
584	            self._byte_flip_stage(tc)
585	            self._arithmetic_stage(tc)
586	            self._interesting_stage(tc)
587	            self._dictionary_stage(tc)
588	            tc.was_fuzzed = True
589	        self.calculate_score(tc)
590	        self._havoc_stage(tc, self.assign_energy(tc))
591	        if self.current_cycle >= 1:
592	            self._splice_stage(tc, self.splice_energy)
593	
594	    def run(self, max_cycles: Optional[int] = None,
595	            max_execs: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
596	        """Main fuzzing loop.
597	
598	        Cycles through the queue in order; entries discovered during a
599	        cycle are scheduled from the next cycle onward. Non-favored seeds
600	        are skipped with probability ``skip_nonfavored_prob`` (75/25
601	        favored priority). The queue is re-culled after every cycle.
602	        """
603	        cycle = 0
604	        while max_cycles is None or cycle < max_cycles:
605	            self.current_cycle = cycle
606	            snapshot = list(self.queue)
607	            for tc in snapshot:
608	                if (max_execs is not None
609	                        and self.fork_server.exec_count >= max_execs):
610	                    self.cull_queue()
611	                    return
612	                has_favored = any(t.is_favored for t in self.queue)
613	                if (not tc.is_favored and has_favored
614	                        and self.rng.rand() < self.skip_nonfavored_prob):
615	                    continue
616	                self.fuzz_one(tc)
617	            self.cull_queue()
618	            cycle += 1

7	class BasicBlock:
8	    """A basic block in the control flow graph."""
9	
10	    def __init__(self, block_id: int, name: str = ""):
11	        self.block_id = block_id
12	        self.name = name or f"bb_{block_id}"

15	class Edge:
16	    """An edge in the control flow graph."""
17	
18	    def __init__(self, edge_id: int, src: int, dst: int,
19	                 is_crash: bool = False, is_rare: bool = False):
20	        self.edge_id = edge_id
21	        self.src = src
22	        self.dst = dst
23	        self.is_crash = is_crash
24	        self.is_rare = is_rare
